image_description: A close-up, high-resolution portrait of a male Mallard duck (drake) in profile facing right. The image highlights the iridescent emerald green head, a distinct white neck ring, a bright yellow bill with a black tip and nostril, and dark brown/grey chest plumage. The background is heavily blurred (bokeh), suggesting a shallow depth of field.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with the characteristic yellow coloration and black tip associated with a Mallard drake.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While only the upper torso is visible, the plumage texture appears dense and smooth, consistent with waterproof feathers. The visible portion suggests a compact body structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image perfectly matches the Mallard drake description: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and darker chest/body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely outside the frame of this close-up portrait; they cannot be evaluated.
The wings are folded against the body and largely obscured by the angle and cropping; their full shape and pointedness cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in this head-and-shoulders crop.
